title: Rectified dg model comparison for enriched internal Hom
statement:
Use the universes and dg-category localization $\mathsf{Hqe}$ of [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure], the derived enrichment in the enhanced derived category $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$ of [lem-coef-dg-enrichment-rectification], and the coherent tensor and internal Hom of [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus]. Let $\mathcal J,\mathcal B,\mathcal R_0$ be small dg categories over $\mathbf Z$. Write $\mathcal A\otimes^L\mathcal J=Q\mathcal A\otimes Q\mathcal J$ for the derived tensor, and assume its derived enrichment agrees with the enriched tensor. Suppose given bijections, natural in every small dg category $\mathcal A$,
$$\alpha_{\mathcal A}:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{Hqe}}(\mathcal A,\mathcal R_0)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{Hqe}}(\mathcal A\otimes^L\mathcal J,\mathcal B).$$
Let $\mathcal F=\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)}(\mathcal J,\mathcal B)$, where the inputs denote derived enrichments. There is a small dg rectification $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{dg}}$ of $\mathcal F$ and an equivalence $e:\mathcal R_0\simeq\mathcal F_{\mathrm{dg}}$ in the enhanced localization, identifying the derived mapping objects. Its homotopy class realizes the given representing bijections. In particular the evaluation map obtained from $\alpha_{\mathcal R_0}(1)$ agrees, under $e$, with coherent enriched evaluation up to a homotopy in the enhanced localization.

source.place: Haugseng, Rectification of enriched infinity-categories, Theorem 5.8 and Example 5.11; representing-object comparison combined with the closed tensor in On the tensor product of enriched infinity-categories, Remark 9.5 (https://arxiv.org/html/2311.13362v1). Agent specialization; read online, not archived. No Stacks tag supplies this dg-enriched comparison.

proof.text: Fix the small universe of the hypothesis. Write $L=\mathrm{dgCat}_{\mathbf Z}[\mathrm{qe}^{-1}]_\infty$ and $C=\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)}$. Apply [lem-coef-localization-homotopy-category] to the category of small dg categories and its quasi-equivalences. Its hypothesis is exactly the coherent localization defining $L$; it identifies $hL$ with $\mathsf{Hqe}$, compatibly with dg functors. If needed make that category small in a further universe; the universe-invariance assertion of [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure] preserves the original morphisms and mapping spaces. We henceforth use this identification. In particular $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{Hqe}}(A,B)=\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_L(A,B)$. Naturality stated for strict dg functors also extends to their formally inverted quasi-equivalences: a commuting square of bijections still commutes after inverting its vertical bijections.

source.place: Theorem 1.6.6, Corollary 1.6.8, Remarks 7.1.4 and 7.1.6, printed pp. 24-25 and 324-325; application to dg categories by the agent.

proof.text: Let $E:L\simeq C$ be the equivalence given by [lem-coef-dg-enrichment-rectification]. By [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus], $F=\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)}(EJ,EB)$ is an object of the same category of small enriched categories. Essential surjectivity of $E$ gives a small dg category $F_{\mathrm{dg}}$ and an equivalence $\rho:E(F_{\mathrm{dg}})\simeq F$. Keep this choice fixed. This uses rectification for objects only; no naturality data for the given family $\alpha$ has yet been lifted.

source.place: Theorem 5.8 and Example 5.11, over Z; representing-object specialization by the agent.

proof.text:
Full faithfulness of $E$, postcomposition with $\rho$, and the closed tensor adjunction of [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus] give, naturally in $A$, equivalences of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_L(A,F_{\mathrm{dg}})\simeq\operatorname{Map}_C(EA,F)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_C(EA\otimes EJ,EB)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_L(A\otimes^L J,B).$$
For the last equivalence use exactly the tensor comparison assumed in the item, together with full faithfulness of $E$ from [lem-coef-dg-enrichment-rectification]. The closed adjunction sends $v:EA\to F$ to $\operatorname{ev}\circ(v\otimes1_{EJ})$. Taking connected components gives natural bijections $\beta_A:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{Hqe}}(A,F_{\mathrm{dg}})\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{Hqe}}(A\otimes^L J,B)$; step 1 supplies the identification with these Hom sets. Thus $F_{\mathrm{dg}}$ represents the very same set-valued functor as $R_0$, with the specified evaluation convention.

source.place: Remark 9.5; closed enriched tensor and evaluation, specialized by the agent.

proof.text: Put $\gamma_A=\beta_A^{-1}\alpha_A$, a natural bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}(A,R_0)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(A,F_{\mathrm{dg}})$ in $\mathsf{Hqe}$. Define $e_0=\gamma_{R_0}(1_{R_0})$ and $f_0=\gamma_{F_{\mathrm{dg}}}^{-1}(1_{F_{\mathrm{dg}}})$. Naturality, evaluated on an arrow $u:A\to R_0$, says $\gamma_A(u)=e_0\circ u$. Evaluating on $f_0$ gives $e_0\circ f_0=1_{F_{\mathrm{dg}}}$. Applying the same calculation to the inverse natural family gives $\gamma_A^{-1}(v)=f_0\circ v$ and hence $f_0\circ e_0=1_{R_0}$. These two identities prove that $e_0$ is an isomorphism. Moreover for every $u$ we have $\alpha_A(u)=\beta_A(e_0\circ u)$. This is the full representing-object uniqueness argument, using only naturality, identities and inverses of bijections.

source.place: Agent argument after Theorem 5.8: explicit ordinary representing-object comparison; not a theorem asserted in the paper.

proof.text:
Choose an edge $e:R_0\to F_{\mathrm{dg}}$ representing the class $e_0$ in $hL$. The definition of $hL$ and the equivalence-edge criterion of [lem-coef-localization-homotopy-category] show that this edge exists and is an equivalence, since $e_0$ is invertible. The functor $E$ of [lem-coef-dg-enrichment-rectification] sends $e$ to an enriched equivalence; such equivalences are fully faithful and essentially surjective. Consequently, for all objects $x,y$ of the derived enrichment of $R_0$, the induced map
$$E(R_0)(x,y)\longrightarrow E(F_{\mathrm{dg}})(Ee(x),Ee(y))$$
is an equivalence in $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$. Composing with $\rho$ identifies these with the derived mapping objects of $F$. Thus the mapping-object conclusion follows from an actual enhanced equivalence, rather than from the bijections of Hom sets alone. Its homotopy class realizes $\alpha$ by the last formula in step 4.

source.place: Theorem 1.6.6, Corollary 1.6.8, Remarks 7.1.4 and 7.1.6, printed pp. 24-25 and 324-325; application to dg categories by the agent.

proof.text:
Let $\epsilon_0=\alpha_{R_0}(1_{R_0})$ and choose a representative $\epsilon:R_0\otimes^L J\to B$ in $L$. Step 4 gives $\epsilon_0=\beta_{R_0}(e_0)$. By the explicit closed-adjunction formula in step 3, the latter class is represented, after applying $E$ and the assumed tensor identification, by
$$E(R_0)\otimes EJ\xrightarrow{(\rho\circ E(e))\otimes1}F\otimes EJ\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}}EB.$$
The coherent evaluation and tensoring in this formula are those of [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus]. Their preimage under the fully faithful $E$ has the same class as $\epsilon$ in $hL$. By the homotopy-class description of morphisms in [lem-coef-localization-homotopy-category], they are joined by a homotopy in the mapping space $\operatorname{Map}_L(R_0\otimes^L J,B)$. This proves exactly the asserted evaluation compatibility. No choice of a contractible space of lifts of the family $\alpha$ is asserted or needed.
